In the Supabase SQL editor, run: 1. select tablename from pg_tables where schemaname='public' order by tablename; 2. select tablename, policyname from pg_policies where schemaname='public' order by tablename, policyname; 3. select column_name, data_type from information_schema.columns where table_name='users' and column_name in ('xp','level'); EOF)

Shell(cat > /tmp/strip_policies.py <<'PY' import re import sys path = sys.argv[1] with open(path, 'r') as f: content = f.read() # Find each policy block: from "CREATE POLICY" to its closing ";" # Then remove the block. Also drop preceding "--" comment lines that # are attached to it. lines = content.split('\n') out = [] i = 0 while i < len(lines): line = lines[i] if 'CREATE POLICY' in line: # Find the end of this CREATE POLICY statement (matching ';') depth = 0 end = i started = False for j in range(i, len(lines)): for ch in lines[j]: if ch == '(': depth += 1 started = True elif ch == ')': depth -= 1 if started and depth == 0 and ';' in lines[j]: end = j break if started and depth == 0 and ';' in lines[j]: break # Remove lines i..end # Also drop any preceding "ALTER TABLE ... ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY" lines # (we'll re-enable in security-policies.sql, but skipping them here is fine # because ENABLE is idempotent.) # Walk backwards to drop preceding comment lines attached to this policy k = i - 1 while k >= 0 and lines[k].strip().startswith('--'): k -= 1 # If the previous line is also a CREATE POLICY / ALTER / nothing special, # leave the comment lines as-is. Easier: just drop only the policy block. i = end + 1 continue if 'ALTER TABLE' in line and 'ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY' in line: # Skip this line i += 1 continue out.append(line) i += 1 # Collapse runs of 3+ blank lines into 2 final = [] blank_run = 0 for line in out: if line.strip() == '': blank_run += 1 if blank_run <= 2: final.append(line) else: blank_run = 0 final.append(line) with open(path, 'w') as f: f.write('\n'.join(final)) print(f"Stripped policies. New line count: {len(final)}") PY python3 /tmp/strip_policies.py /mnt/storage/Projects/BrickByBrick/supabase/schema.sql)
